html:
Jeltoqsan, Kazakh for "December", was a wave of protests in Alma-Ata (Almaty), capital of Soviet Kazakhstan, from 16 to 19 December 1986.

They began when Mikhail Gorbachev removed Dinmukhamed Kunaev, the long serving Kazakh head of the republic's Communist Party, and replaced him with Gennady Kolbin, a Russian with no ties to Kazakhstan. Thousands of young Kazakhs, many of them students, gathered on the city's main square to protest.

Troops and police broke up the crowds with clubs, dogs and water cannon. Some people were killed, though the number is still disputed, and many were arrested, expelled from university or jailed. It was one of the first ethnic protests of the Gorbachev years and a warning of the national tensions that would help break up the Soviet Union. In 1989 Kolbin was replaced by Nursultan Nazarbayev. Kazakhstan declared independence on 16 December 1991, five years to the day after the protests began.
sum: Jeltoqsan, Kazakh for "December", was a wave of protests in Alma-Ata (Almaty), capital of Soviet Kazakhstan, from 16 to 19 December 1986.
